chunks: As for what al-Husayn ibn Sa'id narrated from Fadalah, from Ibn Sinan, from Abi 'Abdillah عليه السلام, he said:
The Friday prayer is not valid except for one who has attended the two sermons.

So the correct understanding of this report is that it is not fully meritorious and complete except for one who has attended the two sermons, and by that he did not intend to negate sufficiency, according to what he explained in the first two reports; and this further clarifies that.

key_terms.الْخَبَرَيْنِ الْأَوَّلَيْنِ: the first two reports previously cited for clarification
key_terms.الْخُطْبَتَيْنِ: the two sermons delivered before Jumu'ah prayer
key_terms.نَفْيَ الْإِجْزَاءِ: negation of legal sufficiency or validity

ai.seo_question: Does missing the two sermons invalidate Jumu'ah, or does it only reduce its completeness?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling of Jumu'ah in relation to catching the two sermons. It explains that attendance at both sermons pertains to the complete merit and perfection of the Friday prayer, not necessarily to the negation of its legal sufficiency, as clarified by the earlier reports.
